title: Blender interstitial volume: A novel virtual measurement of structural complexity applicable to marine benthic habitats
author: Sadchatheeswaran, Moloney, et al.

steps.title: Install Blender and Measure Panel
steps.instruction: Download Blender 2.74, unzip (if zip), open blender.exe, dismiss welcome screen, set engine to “Cycles Render”, enable Emulate 3 Button Mouse, Continuous Grab, Select with Right, Emulate Numpad (if needed), then open User Preferences, add Measure Panel add‑on, activate it, toggle Object Properties (N), click Activate → Measure, enable Volume, set Global, verify default cube shows volume 8.00000 (8 cm³). Change scene units to Metric, Degrees, set scale to 0.01 so the default cube dimensions read 2 cm and volume 8 cm³.

substeps.instruction: 1. Download Blender 2.74 from http://download.blender.org/release/Blender2.74/ (zip or exe).
2. Move file to chosen folder and unzip if needed.
3. Open blender‑2.74‑[OS]/blender.exe; click screen to close welcome.
4. In the main window: go to File > User Preferences → Input tab; check Emulate 3 Button Mouse, Continuous Grab, Select with Right, Emulate Numpad (if no numpad).
5. In the same window go to System tab and change Engine to “Cycles Render”.
6. In User Preferences → Add‑ons tab, search “Measure Panel”, check 3D View: Measure Panel, click Save User Settings, close preferences.
7. Press N to open the right‑hand Object Properties panel, scroll to bottom, click Activate next to Measure, expand Measure shelf, uncheck Draw distance, check Volume, ensure Global is selected.
8. Verify default cube shows “Cube: 8.00000” (volume 8 cm³).
9. Open Properties panel (right side), click Scene icon, under Units set Unit System to Metric, Angle to Degrees, Scale to 0.01.
10. Return to Object Properties; under Transform > Dimensions the cube reads 2 cm, under Measure the volume reads 8 cm³.

steps.title: Create 3D Models of Engineers and Substrate
steps.instruction: Model a barnacle (≈2 cm³), a mussel (≈2 cm³), a funnel (10 × 10 × 20 cm), a plane (10 × 10 cm, optional bumpy topography), and a surrounding sphere (20 cm diameter, 32 segments/rings). Keep objects non‑manifold, low‑vertex, and save frequently.

substeps.instruction: Barnacle:
a. Move default cube to a new layer (M → choose empty box).
b. If needed, add a new cube (Shift + A → Mesh > Cube) and set dimensions to 2 × 2 × 2 cm in Object Properties → Transform → Dimensions.
c. With cube selected, add Subdivision Surface modifier (Properties → Modifiers → Add Modifier > Subdivision Surface), set View and Render subdivisions to 1.
d. Switch to Edit Mode (Tab).
e. Ensure vertex select mode (icon bottom‑left). Use orthogonal front view (Numpad 5 + 1).
f. Change shading to Wireframe (Z).
g. Add two horizontal edge loops (Ctrl + R), confirm with mouse‑wheel or PgUp for two cuts, left‑click to place, then left‑click again to confirm.
h. Scale the new loops on Z axis (S → Z) until they sit near top and bottom of the cube.
i. Deselect all (A), box‑select top 8 vertices (B).
j. Scale those vertices inward (S) to shorten the top, then move them down (G → Z) to reduce height.
k. Return to Object Mode, click Apply on Subdivision Surface modifier.
l. Rename object to “Barnacle” in Outliner (right‑click > Rename).
Mussel:
a. Move Barnacle aside (G → X).
b. Center 3D cursor (Shift + C).
c. Add UV Sphere (Shift + A → Mesh > UV Sphere), set Segments = 8, Rings = 8.
d. In Object Mode, scale sphere on Y axis (S → Y) to flatten.
e. Enter Edit Mode, enable Proportional Editing (Connected) (icon bottom), ensure no vertices selected (A).
f. Box‑select bottom vertex (B), drag it down (G → Z).
g. Increase influence radius with mouse wheel or PgUp/PgDn until shape resembles a mussel, left‑click to confirm.
h. Scale bottom vertex inward (S) to create umbo.
i. Scale whole object in Object Mode to achieve volume ≈2 cm³ if needed.
j. Rename object to “Mussel”.
Funnel:
a. Add Cube (Shift + A → Mesh > Cube), set dimensions to 10 × 10 × 20 cm in Object Properties.

b. Switch to Edit Mode, disable Proportional Editing, select top four vertices, extrude upward (E), then scale outward (S) to create a wider top; size is not critical, just enough space for ~20 mussels.
c. Rename to “Funnel”.
Plane:
a. Add Plane (Shift + A → Mesh > Plane), set dimensions to 10 × 10 cm.
b. If bumpy topography desired, stay in Edit Mode, Subdivide (W > Subdivide) with 10 cuts, set Fractal = 0.017.
Surrounding Sphere:
a. Add UV Sphere, set Segments = 32, Rings = 32, scale to 20 cm diameter (Object Properties → Dimensions).
General:
- Save frequently (File > Save or Ctrl + S).
- Keep vertex count low; avoid faces with >4 edges (non‑manifold objects cannot be measured).

steps.title: Attach Encrusting Engineers – Basic
steps.instruction: Place barnacles on the plane, duplicate to the desired count (example 10), then arrange or randomize their positions while keeping them on the plane surface.

substeps.instruction: 1. Select Barnacle and Plane, ensure both are on the same layer.
2. Position Barnacle on top of the plane (check in top view Numpad 7).
3. Duplicate Barnacle ten times:
a. Use Shift + D, drag each copy onto the plane; repeat for all ten.
b. Alternatively, use an Array modifier: in Properties → Modifiers, add Array, set Fit Type = 10, Apply, then in Edit Mode separate into ten objects (P > By Loose Parts).
4. Give each Barnacle its own origin (Shift + Ctrl + Alt + C → Origin to Geometry).
5. Arrange barnacles manually (G to move in top view) or randomize:
a. Select all ten barnacles, press Space, type “Randomize Transform”, press Enter.
b. In Tools panel set Randomize X/Y to 2–4 cm.
c. If any barnacles lifted off the plane, move them back (G).
6. Ensure all barnacles sit on the plane surface (front view Numpad 1, move Z with G → Z if needed).

steps.title: Attach Encrusting Engineers – Advanced
steps.instruction: Use a particle system on the plane to distribute barnacle clones, then convert particles to real objects and verify volumes.

substeps.instruction: 1. Prepare parent barnacle:
a. In Edit Mode, move the barnacle’s origin to its bottom (Shift + Ctrl + Alt + C → Origin to Geometry, then move origin down).
b. Rename to “parent barnacle”.
2. Select Plane, open Properties → Particles, click New:
a. Set Type to Hair, check Advanced.
b. Number = 10 (or desired count).
c. Emission > Emit From: Faces, Distribution: Random.
d. Physics > Size = 0.25.
e. Render > Render As: Object, Dupli Object = parent barnacle, enable Rotation and Scale.
f. Adjust Seed to randomize placement.
3. If orientation wrong, select parent barnacle, go to Edit Mode, rotate 90° clockwise (Front view Numpad 1, R → 90).
4. Convert particle system to mesh objects:
a. With Plane selected, go to Properties → Modifiers → Convert (or use Object > Convert > Mesh).
5. Delete particle system and parent barnacle (Properties → Particles, click ‘‑’).
6. Verify each barnacle’s volume remains ≈2 cm³ (Measure panel), scale individually if needed.

steps.title: Drop Mobile Engineers onto Plane
steps.instruction: Place funnel and mussel, set physics for mussel, animate to let mussels settle, duplicate mussels to desired number (example 20), randomize their positions and orientations, and capture the final frame (300).

substeps.instruction: 1. Add Funnel and Mussel to same layer as Plane and Barnacles:
a. Move Funnel over the plane so the plane lies inside the funnel.
b. Place Mussel object near the top of the funnel.
2. Set mussel physics:
a. Change render engine to “Blender Game”.
b. In Properties → Physics, set Physics Type to Rigid Body.
c. Collision Bounds → Bounds: Convex Hull, Margin: 0.
d. Test run animation (P), stop with Esc.
3. Duplicate mussels to match sample size (example 20):
a. Add Array modifier to mussel, Fit Type = 20, Apply.
b. In Edit Mode, separate individual mussels (P > Separate by Loose Parts).
c. Give each mussel its own origin (Shift + Ctrl + Alt + C → Origin to Geometry).
4. Randomize mussel placement:
a. Select all mussels, press Space, type “Randomize Transform”, press Enter.
b. Set random location range to ±3 cm in X, Y, Z and rotation range to 180° in all axes.
5. Run animation until mussels settle:
a. In Game menu, enable Record Animation.
b. Play animation (P) until all mussels lie on the plane and stop moving.
c. Press Esc to stop, note Timeline Current Frame = 300.

steps.title: Measure Solid Sample Volume
steps.instruction: Join all ecosystem‑engineer objects, clear any animation keyframes, centre the origin, and record the combined solid volume.

substeps.instruction: 1. Move Funnel to a separate layer (M, choose empty box).
2. Select all engineer objects (Barnacle, Mussel, etc.), ensure one is active (yellow outline), join with Ctrl + J.
3. Clear keyframes:
a. In Object Properties, right‑click the yellow bars under Location and Rotation, choose Clear Keyframes (bars turn grey).
4. Centre origin of the joined object (Shift + Ctrl + Alt + C → Origin to Geometry).
5. Measure volume via Measure panel – example recorded volume = 60.21 cm³.
Note: Measure near the grid origin to avoid small location‑dependent errors.

steps.title: Measure Shrinkwrap Volume
steps.instruction: Enclose the solid sample with a sphere, shrinkwrap it to the sample, record that volume, then expand the shrinkwrap to approximate epifauna space and record the expanded volume.

substeps.instruction: 1. Join engineers and the funnel (if not already) with Ctrl + J, rename final object “Sample 1”.
2. Add surrounding sphere (already created, 20 cm diameter, 32 segments/rings).
a. Move sphere to same layer (M), position it (G) so it fully encloses Sample 1.
3. Shrinkwrap:
a. In Properties → Modifiers, add Shrinkwrap modifier.
b. Set Target = Sample 1, then click Apply.
c. Record shrinkwrap sphere volume – example 109.19 cm³.
4. Expand shrinkwrap to simulate epifauna:
a. Select shrinkwrapped sphere, enter Edit Mode.
b. Execute sequence:
- E + Enter + S + 1.1 + X + Enter
- E + Enter + S + 1.1 + Y + Enter
- E + Enter + S + 1.05 + Z + Enter
c. Separate the expanded object (P > Selection).
d. In Object Mode, centre its origin (Shift + Ctrl + Alt + C → Origin to Geometry).
e. Record expanded shrinkwrap volume – example 152.93 cm³.

steps.title: Calculate Interstitial Volume
steps.instruction: Subtract the solid sample volume from the expanded shrinkwrap volume to obtain the Blender interstitial volume.

substeps.instruction: Blender interstitial volume = Expanded shrinkwrap volume (152.93 cm³) – Solid sample volume (60.21 cm³) = 92.72 cm³.
